title: Leadership, autonomy, and how we work together
vimeoName: Belong School · Module 12 · How We Lead

segments.text: Last module, and I've saved the most important conversation for the end:
how we work together. Not the org chart, the real thing.
What I believe about leading people, what I expect from you, and what you have
every right to expect from me. Let me start with a confession.
Nobody taught me hospitality management.
I was a lawyer who fell in love with a field of carnations.
Almost everything I know about running this place, I learned by doing it and by
getting it wrong first. So when I talk about mistakes, I'm not being generous from
some throne of perfection. I'm speaking as this company's most experienced maker of
mistakes. Here is my first principle: I'd rather correct your decision than
make all the decisions. You are the person on the ground, in front of the guest,
with the pan on the fire, with the room to prepare.
You see things I will never see from Lisbon or from a spreadsheet.
If you wait for permission for every judgment call, we become slow and worse.
You stop thinking, because why think when someone above you does it for you?
So the rule is when the guest is in front of you and something needs solving, solve
it. Use the values as your compass.
The long game, the relationship, the coherence between what we say and what we do.
If your solution costs a bottle of wine or a free dessert to save a guest's
evening, do it. Tell your manager after.
I will never, ever punish someone for a generous decision made in good faith for a
guest. Never.
Second principle. The mistake is not the problem. Hiding it is.
In eight years of building and eight more of operating, I've seen every kind of
mistake. Doubles booked, dishes burnt, reservations lost, pipes open
at the wrong moment. Here's what I know. A mistake caught early is an anecdote.
A mistake hidden is a crisis. So the deal between us is this.
You bring me the problem while it's small, and I bring you calm, help, and zero
drama. You hide it until it explodes, and then we have two problems, and the second
one is trust. Speak early. Always.
This applies upward too, by the way. When I'm wrong, tell me.
I promise you it won't be career limiting.
The people who've challenged me best are the people I trust most today. Third.
Standards are how we respect each other. I ask a lot. You know this.
The details, the coherence, the promise-keeping.
Module 6 wasn't gentle. But understand why.
High standards are a form of respect.
Respect for the guests who paid us their trust.
Respect for the colleague whose work your work either lifts or undermines.
Because in a place like this, everything touches everything.
A late room delays a check-in, delays dinner, sours an evening.
And respect for yourself. Nobody feels proud going home from sloppy work, and pride
in work is one of the great pleasures of life.
I want Raverello to be the hardest job some of you ever love. Fourth.
We grow people, not just vegetables.
The regeneration we preach for soil applies to careers.
I want people from São Teotónio and Odemira to build real professional lives here
without leaving their land. That's social sustainability with names
and faces. If you want to learn another section, another skill, wine,
English, numbers, say so. The person cleaning houses today can be running
housekeeping in three years. Versions of that sentence have already come true here
more than once. My commitment. We will always prefer to promote from within,
and your ambition is welcome here.
What I ask in return is that you teach others what you learn.
Knowledge that stays in one head is knowledge the team doesn't have.
Fifth, and this one goes both directions. Well-being is non-negotiable.
I said it in the values module, and I'll close with it.
This industry has a long, ugly tradition of burning people out and calling it
fashion. Not here. Not on my watch.
Breaks are real, days off are real, the schedule is human, and if it ever
isn't,
escalate it. To me, if needed.
I would rather run at slightly lower capacity than run on exhausted people, because
exhausted people can't give warmth, and warmth is our entire product.
And between yourselves, watch out for each other.
Cover for the colleague having a hard week. They'll cover you in yours.
The team is the first community we regenerate. Let me land this whole thing.
Sixteen years ago, there was a field of carnations and a lawyer with a dream that
most sensible people found ridiculous.
Today, there are 38 houses full of stories, a farm that feeds hundreds of people a
week, a beach bar on the sand, a table inside a museum in Lisbon, weddings
under our pines, and a team, you, that carries all of it.
None of it was inevitable. All of it came from believing that a place well cared
for cares for those who inhabit it.
And then working season after season as if that were true.
It turned out it was. You are part of that now. Not employed by it.
Part of it. And my deepest hope for your time here is the same
thing we promise the guests. Because it turns out the brand was never just for
them. Fica. Pertence. Stay. Belong.
Thank you for listening to all of this.
Now,
let's get to work.
